Florida Business and Finance Exam - Online Exam Prep Course [Construction Contractors]

The Florida Business and Finance Exam - Online Exam Prep Course [Construction Contractors] is designed for contractor candidates preparing for the business and financial management portion of the Florida construction licensing exam process. This course focuses on the business side of contracting, including financial management, accounting concepts, contract documents, administrative responsibilities, Florida contractor law, and the reference navigation skills needed for an open book test.

For many Florida construction contractor applicants, the Business and Finance exam is one of the most important parts of the licensing journey. Trade knowledge matters, but the state also expects contractors to understand how to operate a construction business responsibly. That includes managing money, understanding contracts, reading required references, following licensing rules, maintaining proper records, and recognizing the legal and administrative responsibilities that come with contracting work in Florida.

This online exam prep course helps you study with structure instead of guessing where to begin. The goal is to help you become more comfortable with the approved reference materials, understand the way exam questions are built, and practice locating information efficiently during the test. Since the Florida Business and Finance Exam is open book, preparation is not only about memorizing facts. It is also about knowing where information is located, how to use your books under time pressure, and how to connect business concepts to exam-style questions.

Contractor candidates preparing for general, building, residential, and many specialty contractor license categories often need the Business and Finance portion as part of their state exam path. This course supports that preparation by organizing the major business and financial topics into a practical study plan. You will work through concepts tied to accounting, contracting business operations, bidding, contract documents, Florida statutes, administrative duties, employment responsibilities, and compliance topics that are commonly part of contractor business education.

The course is especially useful for students who already have field experience but need a stronger test-preparation system. Many experienced contractors understand jobsite work but have not taken a timed licensing exam in years. Others may know how to run parts of a business but need help reading and navigating the required books quickly. This Florida Business and Finance Exam prep course bridges that gap by focusing on study organization, reference familiarity, and exam confidence.

Instead of treating the exam like a general business class, the course is built around contractor licensing preparation. The examples, study flow, and review approach are focused on the realities of construction contracting. That means attention is given to job cost thinking, business records, tax and payroll concepts, construction contract documents, statutory responsibilities, financial decision-making, and the administrative side of operating as a contractor in Florida.

Exam Details

The Florida Business and Finance Exam is administered as a computer-based test for construction contractor candidates. The exam is multiple choice, and questions use four answer choices. The Business and Finance exam consists of 120 scored questions, with 6.5 hours allotted for the standard Business and Finance examination. The Business and Finance Service Pool examination is a separate version with 60 scored questions and a 3.5-hour time limit.

The Florida construction contractor examination program is connected to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and the Construction Industry Licensing Board. Professional Testing, Inc. handles examination registration, development, and scoring for the construction examinations. After approval, computer-based testing is scheduled through Pearson VUE.

The passing score for Florida construction examinations is 70 percent. Scores are reported as percentage scores, and construction exam scores are not rounded to the nearest percent. Candidates receive an official exam result report after completing the examination.

Division I contractor candidates, including General, Building, and Residential contractor candidates, must pass three examination parts: Business and Finance, Contract Administration, and Project Management. Division II contractor candidates generally must pass Business and Finance and the required trade knowledge examination for the license category. The exact examination parts depend on the license being pursued and whether the candidate already holds another qualifying construction license.

The Business and Finance exam is focused on business and financial management rather than hands-on trade performance. Candidates should expect the exam to test business judgment, contractor administrative knowledge, accounting-related concepts, contract document awareness, Florida law references, and the ability to find information in the allowed books. Basic mathematics is also part of the construction examination expectations.

Because the exam is timed, a strong study plan should include more than reading. Candidates benefit from learning where key information appears in the reference books, practicing exam-style questions, reviewing common terminology, and building a rhythm for moving through questions without losing too much time on any single item.

Open Book Test

The Florida construction examinations are open book examinations. For the Florida Business and Finance Exam, only the approved books listed for the exam may be brought into the testing room. This makes reference preparation a major part of exam readiness.

Open book does not mean unlimited materials. Candidates must bring only the books allowed for the exam. Only one copy of each reference is allowed into the examination site. Original edition reference materials are required unless a reference list specifically allows a PDF version. Bound PDF copies may be permitted only when the reference list allows them, and all reference materials must remain bound during the exam.

Reference materials may contain underlining with pen or highlighter. Handwritten and typewritten notes are not allowed. Existing handwritten notes must be removed or blackened out so they cannot be read. Moveable tabs, such as Post-it style flags, are not allowed. Candidates are not permitted to make marks in the references during the examination.

This course helps students prepare for the open book format by focusing on organization, book navigation, and practical review. On an open book exam, the strongest candidates are usually not the ones who try to memorize every page. They are the candidates who understand the structure of the books, know the subject areas, and can move quickly from a question to the correct reference section.

Licensing Steps

The Florida contractor licensing process depends on the license category, but the exam path generally begins with understanding which examination parts are required for the credential being pursued. Candidates seeking to sit for Florida construction examinations apply directly with Professional Testing, Inc. for the exam process.

After the candidate is approved to test, the candidate may schedule the computer-based examination through Pearson VUE. Candidates taking a computer-based examination are required to provide scheduling information and payment when reserving the exam appointment. Test appointments are based on seating availability at approved testing locations.

On exam day, candidates must bring proper identification and follow the testing center rules. Two forms of valid signature identification are required, and one must be government issued. Acceptable identification examples include a driver’s license, state identification card, passport, or military identification card. The name and address must match the information submitted with the examination application.

After passing the required examination parts, candidates continue with the applicable licensing process through the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation. Passing the exam is an important requirement, but it is not the same as receiving the license. The license application process may include additional requirements based on the license category and the applicant’s status.

This online exam prep course is built for the exam-preparation stage of that process. It helps candidates study the business and finance material before sitting for the examination, so they can approach the test with a clearer plan and stronger understanding of the references.

State Requirements

Florida construction contractor candidates must pass the required examinations for the license category they are pursuing. The Business and Finance exam is a core examination part for Florida construction contractor licensing, and many candidates across Division I and Division II license categories must complete it as part of their exam requirements.

Division I candidates, including General Contractor, Building Contractor, and Residential Contractor candidates, are required to pass Business and Finance, Contract Administration, and Project Management. Division II candidates are generally required to pass Business and Finance and the applicable trade knowledge examination for the specialty or trade category.

The Florida Business and Finance Exam is intended to measure knowledge connected to responsible contractor business operation. Contractors are expected to understand business structure, financial practices, contracts, administrative duties, regulatory compliance, and other responsibilities that affect the public, customers, workers, and the construction industry.

Candidates should prepare with the current examination content information and the reference list that applies to their scheduled examination. Reference lists can change by year, and the books used for the exam must match the applicable examination period. This product page uses the reference titles provided for this course and the Florida Business and Finance exam preparation focus.

Reference Books

The following reference books and documents are connected with preparation for the Florida Business and Finance Exam. These materials support the open book structure of the exam and help candidates study business law, accounting, contractor administration, and contract document topics.

  • Florida Statutes Chapter 455, 2026
    This Florida statute reference supports review of professional regulation, examination administration, and licensing-related statutory material that may apply to Florida contractor exam preparation.
  • Builder’s Guide to Accounting – Revised Edition
    This accounting reference supports study of financial statements, accounting terminology, job cost concepts, payroll-related topics, cash flow, and other financial management areas relevant to operating a construction business.
  • Contractors Manual, 2025
    This contractor business reference supports study of construction business operations, administrative duties, tax and payroll concepts, insurance, licensing-related responsibilities, and other business practices tied to Florida contractor preparation.
  • General Conditions of the Contract for Construction, 2017
    This contract document supports review of general construction contract conditions, project responsibilities, contract administration language, parties to the contract, and procedures commonly used in construction agreements.
  • Standard Form of Agreement between Contractor-Subcontractor, 2017
    This document supports study of contractor and subcontractor agreement terms, responsibilities, payment concepts, scope relationships, and contract coordination issues.
  • Instructions to Bidders, 2018
    This bidding document supports review of bidding procedures, bidder responsibilities, proposal requirements, and administrative steps tied to the construction bidding process.

Test Information and Study Materials

A smart Florida Business and Finance Exam study plan should combine reading, reference navigation, timed practice, and concept review. Since the test is open book, candidates should become familiar with the layout of each approved reference. That includes knowing where accounting topics appear, where statutory language is located, where contract documents address responsibilities, and where business administration topics can be found.

The Business and Finance exam is not only a memory test. It rewards candidates who can read carefully, understand terminology, and identify the best source for an answer. A question about accounting should send the candidate toward the accounting reference. A question about statutory licensing language should lead the candidate toward the Florida statutes. A contract question may require careful review of one of the AIA documents. A business operations question may require navigation through the contractor manual.

Good preparation should also include calculator practice for basic math. Candidates may use calculators that are silent, hand-held, battery-operated, nonprinting, and without an alphabetic keypad. Math preparation should focus on the types of calculations a contractor may encounter in business and finance study, including percentages, markups, cost relationships, payroll-related math, and financial statement interpretation.

Time management is another major part of preparation. A 6.5-hour exam may seem long, but 120 scored questions require steady pacing. Students should practice answering questions, marking difficult items for review, and moving forward instead of getting trapped by one question. The computer-based exam format allows candidates to navigate through questions, mark items for review, and monitor remaining time.

Study materials for this course are designed to help candidates build a repeatable system. That system includes learning the subject areas, reviewing the references, practicing with exam-style questions, and improving speed. The strongest preparation happens when students combine concept understanding with practical book navigation.

For candidates who feel overwhelmed by the reference list, the course helps break the preparation into manageable pieces. Rather than trying to read every book from front to back without a plan, students can focus on the key purpose of each reference. The accounting book supports financial questions. The statutes support legal and regulatory questions. The contractor manual supports business operations and administrative topics. The AIA documents support contract, subcontract, and bidding questions.

How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal

1 Exam Prep helps contractor candidates prepare with organized study guidance, trade-focused review, and a realistic approach to exam readiness. The Florida Business and Finance Exam can feel intimidating because it combines accounting, contracts, statutes, administrative rules, and business operations. A structured online course gives students a clearer path through the material.

The course supports students by organizing the study process around the way contractor candidates actually prepare. Instead of simply handing students a stack of books, 1 Exam Prep helps connect the references to the exam experience. Students learn how to approach open book questions, how to identify the likely reference source, and how to become more comfortable navigating the materials under timed conditions.

Reference navigation is especially important for the Florida Business and Finance Exam. Knowing that an answer is somewhere in the books is not enough. Candidates need practice finding information efficiently. 1 Exam Prep emphasizes study structure, book familiarity, and question practice so students can build confidence before exam day.

The course also helps students focus on the business side of contracting. Many candidates come from strong field backgrounds but need support with accounting terminology, financial statements, payroll concepts, contract language, bidding documents, and licensing law. This exam prep course gives those topics a more organized framework, making it easier to study consistently and identify areas that need more review.

1 Exam Prep does not promise a passing score or guarantee licensing approval. What it does provide is a practical preparation system for serious candidates who want to study with direction. With organized lessons, reference-based review, and practice-oriented preparation, students can approach the Florida Business and Finance Exam with a stronger understanding of what to expect and how to prepare.

FAQ Section

What is the Florida Business and Finance Exam?

The Florida Business and Finance Exam is the business and financial management examination used in the Florida construction contractor licensing process. It focuses on contractor business operations, accounting, contracts, administrative duties, statutory responsibilities, and financial management topics.

Is the Florida Business and Finance Exam open book?

Yes. Florida construction examinations are open book. Candidates may bring only the approved references allowed for the specific examination. The books must follow the testing rules for binding, notes, highlighting, and tabs.

How many questions are on the Florida Business and Finance Exam?

The standard Business and Finance exam has 120 scored multiple-choice questions. The Business and Finance Service Pool exam has 60 scored questions.

How much time is allowed for the exam?

The standard Business and Finance exam allows 6.5 hours. The Business and Finance Service Pool exam allows 3.5 hours.

What score is required to pass?

Florida construction examination scores are reported as percentage scores, and the minimum passing score is 70 percent. Scores are not rounded to the nearest percent.

Who administers the Florida Business and Finance Exam?

Professional Testing, Inc. handles registration, development, and scoring for the Florida construction examinations. After approval, computer-based exams are scheduled and administered through Pearson VUE.

Do I need the reference books for this course?

The Florida Business and Finance Exam is an open book exam built around approved references. Students preparing for the test should study with the applicable reference books and documents for their exam period.

Can I bring handwritten notes into the exam?

No. Handwritten and typewritten notes are not allowed in the reference materials. Underlining with pen or highlighter may be used, but moveable tabs are not allowed and candidates may not write in the references during the exam.

Does this course guarantee that I will pass?

No course can guarantee an exam result. This course is designed to help students prepare through organized study guidance, reference navigation, practice-oriented review, and a structured approach to the Florida Business and Finance Exam.

Is this course only for General Contractor candidates?

No. The Business and Finance exam is used across Florida construction contractor licensing categories. General, Building, Residential, and many specialty contractor candidates may need this exam as part of their licensing path.

Exam Details

The Florida Business and Finance exam is part of the Florida construction contractor examination program. The exam is connected with the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and the Construction Industry Licensing Board. Professional Testing, Inc. handles construction examination registration, development, and scoring, and approved candidates schedule computer-based examinations through Pearson VUE.

The standard Florida Business and Finance exam is a computer-based multiple-choice examination. It includes 120 scored questions and allows 6.5 hours of testing time. A separate Business and Finance Service Pool examination includes 60 scored questions and allows 3.5 hours. The passing score for Florida construction examinations is 70 percent.

The Business and Finance exam measures knowledge of business management and financial management as they apply to construction contracting. Candidates should prepare for questions involving accounting, financial records, business organization, contracts, bidding, licensing responsibilities, insurance concepts, payroll-related topics, administrative duties, and Florida statutory material.

Division I contractor candidates, including General, Building, and Residential contractor candidates, are typically required to pass Business and Finance, Contract Administration, and Project Management. Division II contractor candidates generally take Business and Finance along with the applicable trade knowledge examination for the license classification. The exact exam parts depend on the contractor license category being pursued.

The Business and Finance exam requires more than general business knowledge. Candidates need to understand how business concepts apply to contractors. The exam may involve formal accounting terms, contract document language, statutory references, and administrative procedures. Open Book Test

The Florida Business and Finance exam is an open book test. Candidates may bring approved reference materials into the examination room, but only the references allowed for that exam may be used. The open book format makes book familiarity, reference organization, and time management essential parts of preparation.

Open book does not mean unlimited notes or materials. Exam references must comply with testing rules for approved books, binding, highlighting, notes, and tabs. Only one copy of each reference is allowed in the examination room. Reference books must remain bound during the exam. Handwritten and typewritten notes are not allowed inside the books. Underlining with pen or highlighter may be used, and prohibited notes must be removed or completely blackened out so they cannot be read.

Licensing Steps

The first step is identifying the correct Florida Division II specialty license category. The applicant should determine which classification matches the work being performed. Division II categories are trade-specific, so the applicant’s documented experience should align with the selected license category. Applying for the wrong category can create delays or lead to an application that does not support the applicant’s actual work scope.

The next step is reviewing whether the applicant is pursuing a certified license or a registered license. A certified contractor license is a statewide Florida license. A registered contractor license is connected to a local jurisdiction. The correct route depends on the applicant’s goals, work location, local credential status, examination path, and DBPR application category.

After the license type is identified, the applicant should organize experience documentation. Florida specialty contractor licensing requires the applicant to show qualifying experience for the selected category. Experience records should be clear, consistent, and tied to the specialty trade being requested. Work history, employer information, supervisory roles, project types, dates, and supporting documentation should be organized before the application is submitted.

The applicant should then organize the exam process. Many Division II applicants need the Business and Finance exam plus the specialty trade knowledge exam. Exam registration, approval, scheduling, study preparation, and score tracking should be handled carefully. Passing score records should be kept with the licensing file.

Business structure should be reviewed early. Many applicants intend to qualify a business entity rather than operate only as an individual. The business name used on the application should match the Florida Division of Corporations record, insurance documents, tax records, and any qualifying-agent paperwork. If the applicant is qualifying a Florida LLC or corporation, the entity record should be active and consistent with the license application.

Financial responsibility documents must also be addressed. Florida contractor licensing includes financial responsibility review, which may involve credit reporting, financial information, bonds, or related documents depending on the applicant’s situation and the application path. Applicants should organize these items before submission so the application package does not stall due to missing financial documentation.

Fingerprinting and background-related requirements should be completed according to DBPR instructions. Applicants should keep confirmation records and make sure that personal information is entered consistently across fingerprinting, examination, and licensing documents.

Insurance and workers’ compensation information should be organized before licensure. Contractors may need general liability insurance and workers’ compensation coverage or exemption documentation depending on the business structure and circumstances. Insurance names, business names, and license names should match the application record as closely as possible.

Once the major documents are organized, the license application is prepared and reviewed. A strong application package should use the correct form, consistent names, complete personal and business information, required signatures, required supporting documents, and correct fee handling. Missing signatures, inconsistent business names, incomplete experience records, or missing supporting documents can delay review.

After submission, DBPR and the Construction Industry Licensing Board control the review process. The board or department may request additional documents, clarification, corrections, or updated information. Applicants should respond promptly and keep copies of all submitted materials, notices, approvals, and follow-up correspondence.

It focuses on application path guidance, document organization, experience records, business entity consistency, financial responsibility planning, fingerprinting steps, insurance information, and submission readiness.

What contractor categories are considered Florida Division II?

Florida Division II generally includes specialty contractor categories, such as roofing, air conditioning, mechanical, plumbing, pool and spa, sheet metal, solar, pollutant storage system, specialty structure, and other specialty classifications. The correct category depends on the applicant’s work scope and qualifying experience.

Who regulates Florida Division II contractor licensing?

Florida contractor licensing is regulated by the Department of Business and Professional Regulation through the Construction Industry Licensing Board.

Does this service include the Florida contractor exam?

No. This is an application service. Exam registration, exam fees, exam-prep courses, reference books, tabbing, highlighting, and study materials are separate unless a product listing specifically includes them.

Do Division II applicants need to pass exams?

Many Florida Division II applicants must complete the required examination process, which commonly includes Business and Finance and the trade knowledge exam for the selected specialty category. Applicants should follow the current DBPR and testing-vendor instructions for their specific license path.

Are Florida Division II contractor exams open book?

Florida Division II contractor exams are commonly treated as open-book exams using approved references. Candidates must follow the current exam bulletin and testing instructions for the specific books, editions, tabs, notes, and materials allowed on test day.

Does passing the exam automatically give me a Florida contractor license?

No. Passing required exams does not automatically issue the license. The applicant must also satisfy the license application requirements, submit the correct application, provide supporting documentation, complete required background steps, address financial responsibility, and receive approval from the proper Florida licensing authority.

Can this service help if I am qualifying a business?

Yes. This service can help organize the application package when the applicant is qualifying a business entity. Business name consistency, entity records, ownership information, qualifying agent details, insurance documents, and application information should be reviewed carefully.

Does this service include business formation?

No. Florida LLC or corporation formation is separate unless a product listing specifically includes business formation. This application service focuses on the contractor license application process.

Does this service include state fees or third-party costs?

No. DBPR fees, exam fees, fingerprinting fees, credit report fees, insurance costs, bond costs, workers’ compensation costs, business filing fees, and other government or third-party charges are separate unless clearly stated in the product listing.

Does this service guarantee my Florida contractor license will be approved?

No. DBPR and the Construction Industry Licensing Board control application review and approval. This service helps prepare and organize the application package, but it does not guarantee approval, processing time, exam results, financial qualification, or licensing outcome.

Can this service help reduce application delays?

This service can help reduce avoidable problems by organizing documents, reviewing common application categories, checking consistency, and helping customers prepare a more complete package. The state still controls review time, deficiency notices, and final decisions.

Is this service useful for applicants who already passed the exam?

Yes. Applicants who have already passed the required exam parts may still need help organizing the license application, financial responsibility documents, business information, fingerprints, insurance records, and supporting materials before submission.

Is this service useful for applicants who have not taken the exam yet?

Yes. Applicants who are still preparing for exams can use this service to understand the application path and begin organizing the documents needed for licensure. Exam preparation and application preparation often work best when planned together.

Why should I use 1 Exam Prep for application support?

1 Exam Prep works with contractor licensing customers and understands the importance of organized paperwork, consistent business records, exam planning, reference navigation, and clear application preparation. This service helps applicants approach the Florida Division II contractor license process with a more structured plan.

    *Our Application Assistance Fee does NOT include required credit reports or the application processing fee required by the Department of Business and Professional Regulations (DBPR). Separate check(s) or money order(s) made payable to the DBPR will be required to submit your application(s).

    **The Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulations (DBPR) requires any contractor who does not have final approval in business matters to appoint a Financially Responsible Officer (FRO). Should you require the designation of a FRO, a separate Financially Responsible Officer Application must be filed with the state.  

    ***Applicants may be exempt from the Florida examinations if you 1) have previously held a valid local license or competency card in any Florida jurisdiction as of June 30, 2021; 2) have had no pending discipline on said license or competency card and has not had said license or competency card disciplined within the last five (5) years; AND 3) have passed a written examination that complies with Rule 61G4-16.009(5)(c), F.A.C., to obtain said license or competency card.

Florida Roofing Contractor Trade Exam - Online Exam Prep Course

Prepare for the Florida Roofing Contractor Trade Exam with structured online exam preparation from 1 Exam Prep. Designed for roofing professionals, construction supervisors, experienced roofers, and individuals pursuing Florida Certified Roofing Contractor licensure, this course focuses on roofing systems, installation methods, technical reference navigation, estimating, construction safety, and Florida building code requirements.

Florida Roofing Contractor examination preparation involves much more than understanding how to install roofing materials. Candidates must develop knowledge of membrane roofing, metal panel systems, spray polyurethane foam roofing, steep-slope assemblies, architectural sheet metal, waterproofing, reroofing, estimating, workplace safety, and construction requirements associated with Florida's demanding weather conditions.

The Florida Roofing Contractor Online Exam Prep Course helps students organize these subjects into a practical study plan. Instead of attempting to memorize every technical manual, candidates learn to recognize the subject of a question, select the appropriate reference, locate supporting information, and apply the relevant requirements.

Roofing construction involves different systems, materials, attachment methods, and installation conditions. Understanding which publication covers each roofing subject is essential when preparing for an open-book contractor examination.

A question involving membrane roofing may require a different technical manual from one involving metal panels, shingles, waterproofing, or architectural sheet metal. Estimating questions may involve mathematical calculations, while safety questions require familiarity with federal construction regulations.

Through organized trade review, reference-book overviews, navigation practice, and test-taking strategies, 1 Exam Prep supports candidates as they develop a more structured approach to roofing examination preparation.

PACKAGE INCLUSION: This package includes ONLINE EXAM PREPARATION ONLY, focused on roofing trade knowledge, reference-book overviews, roofing estimating, code and safety review, open-book navigation, and examination preparation strategies.

IMPORTANT NOTE: THIS PACKAGE DOES NOT INCLUDE ANY PHYSICAL BOOKS. The 11 reference publications listed below are separate study materials and can be purchased separately.

Exam Details

The Florida Roofing Contractor Trade examination evaluates knowledge associated with roofing construction, installation, repair, maintenance, reroofing, waterproofing, estimating, safety, and applicable Florida building code requirements.

This online course focuses on the roofing trade examination. Business and Finance is a separate examination area and is not included as part of this trade-focused preparation.

Roofing contractor candidates must become familiar with several different roofing systems and the technical publications used to describe their materials, installation methods, performance requirements, and construction practices.

Important roofing trade examination subjects include:

  • Membrane Roofing Systems: Built-up roofing, modified bitumen, thermoset membranes, thermoplastic membranes, and related low-slope roofing applications.
  • Metal Panel Roofing: Metal roofing materials, panel configurations, fasteners, clips, attachment methods, sealants, and thermal movement.
  • Spray Polyurethane Foam Roofing: Spray foam applications, protective coatings, substrates, installation practices, and repair considerations.
  • Steep-Slope Roofing: Asphalt shingles, tile, slate, wood roofing products, underlayments, ventilation, and roof covering installation.
  • Architectural Sheet Metal: Copings, gutters, downspouts, flashing, roof edges, transitions, joints, and related metal components.
  • Waterproofing: Above-grade and below-grade systems, substrates, drainage, terminations, penetrations, and protective materials.
  • Reroofing: Existing roof conditions, repair considerations, replacement procedures, and applicable construction requirements.
  • Roofing Estimating: Measurements, roof area, slope calculations, materials, labor, waste allowances, and project-cost calculations.
  • Roofing Safety: OSHA construction requirements, fall protection, ladders, scaffolds, tools, and personal protective equipment.
  • Florida Building Code: Roofing materials, roof assemblies, weather protection, structural considerations, wind resistance, and inspections.
  • High-Velocity Hurricane Zones: Testing procedures and technical requirements associated with roofing products and assemblies.
  • Moisture and Airflow: Condensation, air leakage, roof assembly performance, and related construction considerations.

The examination preparation process requires candidates to connect technical knowledge with the appropriate reference. Understanding the differences among roofing systems can help students determine which publication is most relevant to a question.

Florida construction examinations, other than plumbing, are administered through computer-based testing. Candidates register through Professional Testing, Inc. and, after authorization, schedule their examination through Pearson VUE.

Open Book Test

The Florida Roofing Contractor Trade examination uses an open-book testing format. Candidates may bring authorized reference publications into the applicable examination session when those materials comply with current testing requirements.

Open-book examinations require preparation and efficient reference navigation. Having several books available does not automatically make questions easier. Candidates must recognize the roofing subject, select the correct publication, locate the relevant provision, and interpret the information accurately.

For example, membrane roofing questions may require the NRCA Roofing Manual covering membrane systems. Metal panel or spray polyurethane foam questions may involve a different NRCA publication, while architectural sheet metal questions may involve the SMACNA manual.

Estimating questions may require Walker's Building Estimator's Reference Book or Roofing Construction and Estimating. Safety questions may involve OSHA 29 CFR Part 1926, while Florida code questions may require the applicable Florida Building Code publication.

Recommended open-book examination strategies include:

  1. Identify the Roofing Subject: Determine whether the question involves roofing systems, materials, installation, estimating, safety, or building codes.
  2. Select the Appropriate Reference: Choose the publication most closely associated with the subject.
  3. Locate Supporting Information: Use indexes, tables of contents, technical figures, chapters, and code sections.
  4. Review Applicability: Check definitions, installation conditions, notes, and related technical provisions.
  5. Evaluate the Answer: Compare the reference information with the question and available answers.
  6. Maintain Examination Pace: Avoid excessive searching after identifying the relevant requirement.

Current examination rules permit approved references containing highlighting or underlining. Handwritten and typewritten notes are not permitted. Moveable tabs are prohibited, and candidates may not mark reference materials during testing. Only one copy of each approved publication may be brought into the testing site.

Students should practice with their reference books throughout preparation and organize their study around the materials permitted for their scheduled examination.

Licensing Steps

Florida Certified Roofing Contractor candidates must complete the applicable examination, qualification, and licensing requirements before receiving authorization to perform regulated roofing contracting work.

General licensing steps include:

  1. Review License Qualifications: Understand the experience, education, financial responsibility, background, insurance, and application requirements associated with Florida Roofing Contractor certification.
  2. Confirm Required Examinations: Identify the applicable roofing trade examinations and separate Business and Finance requirements.
  3. Register for Examinations: Complete the applicable examination registration process through Professional Testing, Inc.
  4. Obtain Reference Books: Purchase the relevant roofing manuals, estimating publications, OSHA regulations, and Florida code references separately.
  5. Begin Online Exam Preparation: Study roofing systems, installation methods, construction safety, estimating, and Florida code requirements.
  6. Practice Reference Navigation: Develop familiarity with selecting and locating information across the roofing reference library.
  7. Schedule Examination Appointments: Complete scheduling through Pearson VUE following authorization.
  8. Complete the Required Examinations: Take the examinations according to the applicable testing procedures.
  9. Submit the Licensure Application: Complete the appropriate Florida Roofing Contractor application with supporting documentation.
  10. Satisfy Remaining Requirements: Complete applicable financial, insurance, background, and administrative requirements.

Passing the required examinations does not automatically issue a Florida Roofing Contractor license. Applicants must complete the licensing process and receive the appropriate approval before performing regulated contracting work.

State Requirements

Florida Certified Roofing Contractor applicants must satisfy the qualification requirements established for the roofing contractor license category.

Applicants generally must document four years of qualifying construction experience or an accepted combination of college education and relevant construction experience.

Qualifying experience must relate to the license category and meet the documentation requirements associated with the selected application pathway.

Additional licensing requirements may involve financial responsibility, background information, insurance, workers' compensation compliance, application documentation, and applicable fees.

Florida Roofing Contractor certification has a defined legal scope involving roofing, waterproofing, and related authorized work. Candidates should understand the activities permitted under the credential and the limitations associated with separately regulated contractor classifications.

Applicants with a qualifying bachelor's degree in building construction from an accredited four-year college and the required grade-point average may qualify for a trade-knowledge examination exemption. Other applicable licensing requirements remain part of the certification process.

Maintaining organized records of employment, project experience, supervisory responsibilities, education, and roofing work can help applicants prepare their supporting documentation.

Reference Books

The Florida Roofing Contractor Trade Exam Online Exam Prep Course is organized around 11 roofing, estimating, safety, and Florida construction code references.

IMPORTANT: These physical reference books are not included with the online exam prep package. They can be purchased separately.

  • Walker's Building Estimator's Reference Book, 33rd Edition, 2024
    A construction estimating reference covering labor, materials, quantities, productivity, project calculations, and practical estimating information.
  • Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926
    Federal OSHA construction safety regulations addressing fall protection, ladders, scaffolds, electrical hazards, protective equipment, tools, and jobsite safety.
  • SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual
    A technical reference covering architectural sheet metal, flashing, copings, gutters, downspouts, roof edges, joints, drainage, and related metal installation details.
  • Roofing Construction and Estimating, 13th Printing, 2022
    Addresses roofing materials, construction methods, roof geometry, measurements, material quantities, labor, estimating procedures, and project planning.
  • NRCA Roofing Manual: Membrane Roofing Systems
    Covers built-up roofing, modified bitumen, thermoset and thermoplastic membrane systems, insulation, roof decks, attachment methods, flashing, drainage, and installation details.
  • NRCA Roofing Manual: Metal Panel and SPF Roof Systems
    Addresses metal panel roofing and spray polyurethane foam systems, including substrates, fasteners, sealants, protective coatings, flashing, attachments, and repairs.
  • NRCA Roofing Manual: Steep-Slope Roof Systems
    Covers shingles, tile, slate, wood roofing, underlayments, ventilation, fastening, flashing, valleys, ridges, hips, and roof penetrations.
  • NRCA Roofing Manual: Architectural Metal Flashing, Condensation and Air Leakage Control, and Reroofing
    Addresses architectural metal details, flashing, moisture movement, condensation, air leakage, roof transitions, and reroofing practices.
  • The NRCA Waterproofing Manual, Second Edition
    A technical waterproofing reference covering systems, substrates, drainage, joints, transitions, penetrations, protection, and above-grade and below-grade applications.
  • Florida Building Code - Building, 2026
    A Florida building code reference addressing roof assemblies, weather protection, reroofing, wind resistance, materials, structural provisions, fire classification, and inspections.
  • Florida Building Code - Test Protocols for High-Velocity Hurricane Zones, 2026
    A Florida code publication addressing testing procedures for roofing products, components, assemblies, and building-envelope systems associated with high-velocity hurricane zones.

Each publication supports a different examination subject. The NRCA manuals address specific roofing systems, while the SMACNA manual supports architectural metal and flashing study.

The estimating references support mathematical and project-cost preparation, OSHA addresses construction safety, and the Florida Building Code publications provide regulatory requirements.

Students should use the reference editions applicable to their scheduled examination and follow the testing provider's rules for permitted materials.

Develop familiarity with the table of contents, index, figures, technical tables, appendices, and chapters in each roofing reference.

Practice selecting the correct reference, locating relevant information, completing calculations, and reviewing answers within planned study periods.

15. Review Incorrect Answers

Analyze mistakes to determine whether the difficulty involved roofing knowledge, reference selection, calculation, interpretation, or time management.

16. Maintain a Consistent Study Schedule

Rotate preparation among roofing systems, waterproofing, estimating, safety, Florida building codes, and high-wind requirements. Revisit difficult subjects regularly.

Consistent study helps candidates connect practical roofing experience with technical publication requirements and develop a more efficient approach to open-book examinations.

Becoming a Florida general contractor requires more than experience supervising construction activities. Contractors must understand construction contracts, interpret plans and specifications, coordinate subcontractors, manage project schedules, evaluate construction methods, and apply the Florida Building Code to different project conditions.

The Florida General Contractor Contract Administration & Project Management Online Exam Prep Course supports preparation for two important licensing examination components. Project Management focuses on construction methods, planning, supervision, scheduling, code requirements, and jobsite operations.

Whether you are reviewing years of field experience or preparing to move into greater construction management responsibilities, this course helps organize a substantial body of examination material into practical, focused study areas.

Exam Details

Florida general contractor certification involves separate examinations covering Contract Administration, Project Management, and Business and Finance. Each examination addresses a different part of the knowledge required to operate and manage a construction business.

This online course focuses on the Contract Administration and Project Management components, with particular attention to their construction references, technical topics, and administrative requirements.

  • License Classification: Florida Certified General Contractor
  • Regulatory Authority: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and Construction Industry Licensing Board

Contract Administration involves construction agreements, bidding, estimating, procurement, contractor responsibilities, payment administration, project documentation, and contractual procedures. Candidates must understand how contractual requirements influence construction activities from project award through completion.

Project Management addresses construction planning, field operations, schedules, structural and architectural systems, building code provisions, subcontractor coordination, safety, and project performance.

Both components require the ability to locate information across numerous construction references and apply it to practical questions. Candidates benefit from learning not only construction terminology but also how different documents relate to one another.

Open Book Test

The Florida General Contractor Contract Administration and Project Management examinations are open-book tests. Candidates may use examination references specifically approved for their scheduled examination and testing format.

An open-book construction examination requires familiarity with multiple reference types. Contract questions may involve AIA documents, project management questions may require technical construction textbooks, and code questions may involve specific Florida Building Code volumes.

Efficient examination preparation involves learning how to identify the relevant subject, select an appropriate reference, locate the information, and interpret it accurately.

Florida publishes separate approved-reference lists for construction examination categories and effective testing periods. References used for personal study are not automatically approved for admission into the examination room.

The 2026 Florida Building Code, Ninth Edition, becomes effective for building regulation on December 31, 2026. Florida also publishes construction examination reference lists with separate effective dates for 2026 and 2027.

Understanding reference organization, contract clauses, textbook indexes, construction tables, illustrations, and code headings is an important part of online examination preparation.

Licensing Steps

Florida certified general contractor licensing is administered through the Department of Business and Professional Regulation and the Construction Industry Licensing Board.

  1. Review General Contractor Qualifications: Understand the education, qualifying experience, financial responsibility, and other requirements for the certified general contractor classification.
  2. Organize Relevant Experience: Prepare documentation supporting construction experience and any qualifying educational background.
  3. Study Contract Administration: Review contracts, project administration, estimating, documentation, and contractual responsibilities.
  4. Study Project Management: Review construction methods, project scheduling, building codes, field coordination, and safety.
  5. Prepare for Business and Finance: Address the separate examination covering contractor business operations and financial responsibilities.
  6. Register for the Required Examinations: Complete the applicable examination registration process through Florida's authorized providers.
  7. Complete the Examinations: Satisfy the examination requirements for general contractor certification.
  8. Submit the Licensing Application: Provide the required documentation to the appropriate Florida licensing authority.
  9. Complete Remaining Licensing Requirements: Satisfy applicable financial, insurance, background screening, and administrative obligations.

Preparation for the Contract Administration and Project Management examinations supports the technical and administrative portion of this process. The Business and Finance examination and all remaining licensing qualifications are separate responsibilities.

State Requirements

Florida general contracting is regulated under Florida construction licensing laws and applicable administrative rules. The certified general contractor classification provides broad contracting authority within the scope established by Florida law.

Contractors must understand the relationship between state licensing requirements, construction contracts, building codes, permitting, project supervision, workplace safety, and financial responsibilities.

The Florida Building Code establishes requirements affecting structural systems, building construction, accessibility, energy conservation, residential work, and existing building improvements.

Contractors must also recognize applicable obligations involving workers, subcontractors, insurance, construction documentation, and project administration.

Successful preparation therefore requires attention to both practical building construction and the business processes that support compliant, organized project delivery.

Exam Details

The Florida Plumbing Contractor Trade Knowledge Examination evaluates knowledge associated with plumbing construction, materials, system installation, technical calculations, and applicable building requirements.

The examination is administered under Florida's contractor certification program, overseen by the Department of Business and Professional Regulation and the Construction Industry Licensing Board.

  • Examination: Florida Plumbing Contractor Trade Knowledge
  • Licensing Authority: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation
  • Licensing Board: Construction Industry Licensing Board
  • Question Format: Multiple choice
  • Examination Format: Open book
  • Trade Examination Delivery: Scheduled paper-and-pencil testing
  • Examination Registration: Professional Testing, Inc.
  • Additional Certification Examination: Business and Finance

Florida's Plumbing Contractor trade examination differs from most other state construction trade examinations because it is administered in scheduled paper-and-pencil sessions rather than regular computer-based appointments.

The Business and Finance examination is a separate computer-based examination component.

Technical preparation should include code interpretation, piping principles, fixture installation, mathematical calculations, safety requirements, and familiarity with specialized plumbing systems.

The online course focuses on the trade examination and its associated plumbing knowledge areas. Business and Finance requires separate preparation.

Open Book Test

The Florida Plumbing Contractor Trade Knowledge Examination is an open-book test. Candidates may consult reference publications authorized for their examination category and scheduled testing period.

Open-book testing requires both plumbing knowledge and effective reference navigation. Candidates must recognize the subject of a question, identify the appropriate publication, locate relevant technical information, and apply the requirement correctly.

For example, drainage questions may involve the Florida Plumbing Code, while fuel gas questions may involve the Florida Fuel Gas Code. Mathematical problems may require pipefitting formulas, measurements, or calculations.

Specialized questions may involve accessibility, medical gas systems, standpipe installations, or solar water heating.

Developing familiarity with indexes, definitions, diagrams, sizing tables, and technical standards is an important part of examination preparation.

Florida publishes official Plumbing Contractor examination reference lists identifying authorized materials. Only approved references may be brought into the testing room.

Students benefit from reviewing technical publications alongside their coursework and practicing how to find information efficiently.

Florida Certified Plumbing Contractor licensing involves examination requirements and professional qualifications established through the Construction Industry Licensing Board.

State Requirements

Florida regulates Plumbing Contractors under Chapter 489 of the Florida Statutes.

The Plumbing Contractor classification covers installing, maintaining, repairing, altering, extending, and, when permitted by law, designing plumbing systems.

The authorized scope includes sanitary and storm drainage, venting, water supply systems, septic tanks, drainage and supply wells, swimming pool piping, irrigation, and solar water heating systems.

Florida Plumbing Contractors may also perform specified work involving natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas, medical gas systems, pressure piping, and related installations within their authorized scope.

Other authorized activities include certain standpipe and fire sprinkler work when permitted by law, specialized piping systems, and excavation incidental to plumbing construction.

Contractors must follow applicable construction codes, approved plans, specifications, safety requirements, and professional regulations.

Certification also involves satisfying applicable experience, examination, financial responsibility, insurance, and administrative requirements.

Licensing Steps

Florida construction contractor licensing is regulated through the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and the Construction Industry Licensing Board. Candidates preparing for the Florida General Contractor Exam should understand that the exam is only one part of the general contractor licensing process.

The process begins with confirming that the general contractor license is the correct classification for the work the candidate intends to perform. General contractor licensure is separate from building, residential, specialty, and trade contractor classifications because it is connected to broad construction responsibility, project management, supervision, code compliance, and contractor-level authority.

After selecting the correct license classification, candidates complete the required examination registration process. Once authorized, candidates schedule the required examination sections through the approved testing process and prepare using the official reference list for each exam section.

Passing the required exam sections is an important licensing step, but Florida contractor licensing also includes additional requirements outside the exam itself. Candidates may need to submit experience documentation, demonstrate financial responsibility, satisfy background-related requirements, provide insurance or workers’ compensation documentation where applicable, and complete the state application process for the license classification.

After licensure, general contractors are responsible for operating within the scope of the license, maintaining proper records, renewing the license as required, following Florida laws and rules, meeting applicable building code requirements, coordinating inspections, supervising construction work, and managing projects professionally. Contract Administration and Project Management preparation supports these responsibilities by reinforcing practical knowledge used throughout a construction project.

Open Book Test

Effective open-book preparation involves knowing how to locate relevant information in mechanical codes, NFPA standards, duct construction manuals, technical textbooks, and industry reference guides.

Florida publishes separate reference lists for Air A and Air B examinations. The state also distinguishes examination reference lists effective in 2026 from those effective beginning January 1, 2027.

The officially listed reference editions determine the basis for examination questions. Different editions may be permitted under the examination rules, but the published edition remains the basis for answering questions.

Florida distinguishes Class A and Class B air conditioning contractor certification through the authorized scope of work established in state law.

Class A Air Conditioning Contractors have a broader HVACR scope involving central air conditioning, refrigeration, heating, ventilation, and associated mechanical systems within the activities authorized by Florida law.

Class B Air Conditioning Contractors are subject to equipment-capacity limitations of 25 tons of cooling and 500,000 Btu of heating in any one system. Additional statutory limits govern specific piping, electrical, and related activities.

Contractors must also understand requirements associated with building permits, mechanical installations, energy conservation, safety, and licensing compliance.

Exam Details

The Florida Plumbing Contractor Trade Knowledge Examination evaluates knowledge associated with plumbing installation, repair, materials, piping systems, codes, and construction practices.

Florida contractor certification is overseen by the Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR) and the Construction Industry Licensing Board.

  • Examination: Florida Plumbing Contractor Trade Knowledge
  • Licensing Authority: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation
  • Licensing Board: Construction Industry Licensing Board
  • Examination Format: Open book
  • Question Type: Multiple choice
  • Trade Examination Delivery: Paper-and-pencil testing
  • Examination Registration: Professional Testing, Inc.
  • Additional Examination: Business and Finance

Unlike Florida's computer-based construction trade examinations, the Plumbing Contractor Trade Knowledge Examination is administered in scheduled paper-and-pencil sessions.

Preparation should include familiarity with residential and commercial plumbing, construction drawings, plumbing calculations, water supply, drainage systems, venting, and specialized piping applications.

Technical questions can require candidates to combine field experience with published plumbing requirements, installation principles, and mathematical problem-solving.

Open Book Test

The Florida Plumbing Contractor Trade Knowledge Examination is an open-book test. Candidates may use reference publications authorized for the Plumbing examination and their scheduled testing period.

Open-book testing involves recognizing the technical issue in a question, selecting the appropriate publication, locating applicable information, and applying the requirement correctly.

For example, questions involving drainage and venting may require plumbing code research, while mathematical questions may require pipefitting calculations.

Other subjects may involve standpipe systems, healthcare facility piping, fuel gas installations, or accessibility requirements.

Effective preparation includes studying code organization, indexes, definitions, illustrations, sizing tables, mathematical formulas, and installation requirements.

Florida publishes official approved-reference lists for Plumbing Contractor examinations. Only publications authorized for the scheduled examination may be used in the testing room.

Organized trade preparation helps candidates connect practical plumbing experience with the technical information addressed during the licensing examination.

State Requirements

Florida regulates Plumbing Contractors under Chapter 489 of the Florida Statutes.

The plumbing contractor classification covers the installation, maintenance, repair, alteration, extension, and legally authorized design of plumbing systems.

The statutory scope includes sanitary and storm drainage, venting systems, public and private water supplies, water and sewer facilities, septic tanks, drainage and supply wells, swimming pool piping, irrigation, and solar water heating systems.

Florida Plumbing Contractors may also perform specified work involving water, natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas, medical gas systems, boilers, pressure piping, and related systems within their authorized scope.

Plumbing contractors must comply with applicable plans, specifications, construction codes, laws, and regulations.

The classification also includes certain excavation activities incidental to plumbing work. Work outside the plumbing classification must be performed by appropriately qualified contractors when required.

Applicants pursuing state certification must satisfy applicable examination, experience, financial responsibility, insurance, and administrative requirements.

Exam Details

The Florida Business and Finance exam is part of the Florida construction contractor examination process. It is used for contractor candidates who need to demonstrate knowledge of business and financial management before moving forward in the licensing process. The examination is administered in a computer-based format and is connected with the Florida construction contractor licensing system.

The standard Florida Business and Finance exam includes 120 scored multiple-choice questions and allows 6.5 hours of testing time. A separate Business and Finance Service Pool examination includes 60 scored questions and allows 3.5 hours. The passing score for Florida construction examinations is 70 percent.

The Business and Finance exam covers business and financial topics that apply to construction contracting. Candidates should prepare for questions involving accounting, business records, financial statements, job cost concepts, payroll-related topics, taxes, insurance concepts, contract documents, bidding procedures, licensing responsibilities, administrative duties, and statutory material.

Division I contractor candidates, including General, Building, and Residential contractor candidates, typically complete Business and Finance, Contract Administration, and Project Management exam parts. Division II contractor candidates generally complete Business and Finance along with the applicable trade knowledge exam for the license classification. The exact examination path depends on the Florida contractor license category being pursued.

This rental package is focused on preparation for the Business and Finance portion. It gives candidates access to the listed references and a business course only self-study program so they can review the material, practice using the books, and prepare for the exam in an organized way.

Open Book Test

The Florida Business and Finance exam is an open book test. Candidates may bring approved references into the exam room, but only the materials allowed for the specific examination may be used. This makes book familiarity an important part of preparation. Candidates should not wait until exam day to open the books for the first time. The references should be used throughout the study process.

Open book testing does not mean the exam is easy. The questions are timed, the books can be detailed, and candidates must be able to find information efficiently. A strong study plan includes learning the structure of each reference, reviewing the table of contents and index, practicing with exam-style questions, and understanding which book applies to each subject area.

Reference materials must comply with testing rules for approved books, binding, highlighting, notes, and tabs. Candidates should make sure their exam-day books follow the rules that apply to the Florida construction examination program. Handwritten and typewritten notes are not allowed inside reference books. Underlining with pen or highlighter may be allowed, but candidates must follow all current testing requirements for book condition and markings.

The rental books in this package support open book preparation by giving students the materials needed to study the exam content and practice reference navigation. The self-study course helps organize that preparation so students can spend their time reviewing the business and finance topics most relevant to the examination.

Licensing Steps

Florida contractor licensing steps vary by license classification, but candidates usually begin by identifying the contractor category they want to pursue and confirming which examination parts are required. Many Florida construction contractor candidates must pass the Business and Finance exam as part of the licensing process.

Candidates apply for the applicable construction examination and, once approved, schedule the computer-based exam through the authorized testing process. Before the exam date, candidates should use their study materials to review business and finance topics, practice open book navigation, and become familiar with the references.

On exam day, candidates must follow all testing center rules. This includes bringing proper identification, arriving with approved reference materials, and complying with the rules for book condition and allowed materials. Candidates should make sure their books are organized and compliant before the appointment.

After passing the required examination parts, candidates continue with the contractor license application process through the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation. Passing an examination is an important step, but it does not automatically issue a license. Additional licensing requirements may apply based on the classification and applicant qualifications.

This books and course rental package supports the exam-preparation stage of the process. It is built for candidates who want access to the listed references and a self-study course while preparing for the Florida Business and Finance exam.

State Requirements

Florida construction contractor candidates must complete the examination requirements assigned to their license category. The Business and Finance exam is a key requirement for many contractor applicants because the state expects licensed contractors to understand the business responsibilities involved in construction contracting.

Contractors must be able to manage financial records, understand business obligations, review contracts, follow regulatory responsibilities, handle administrative duties, and operate in a way that protects customers, workers, subcontractors, and the public. The Business and Finance exam reflects these responsibilities by testing knowledge of contractor business and financial management.

Division I candidates generally complete Business and Finance, Contract Administration, and Project Management. Division II candidates generally complete Business and Finance and the applicable trade knowledge examination. Candidates should prepare for the examination parts required for their specific license classification.

The Business and Finance exam supports Florida’s focus on responsible contractor business operation. Candidates should be prepared to work with accounting concepts, contract documents, bidding instructions, statutory references, and business management topics. Exam Details

The Florida Electrical Contractors Certification examination is administered in two parts: a Business examination and a Technical and Safety examination. Both parts are offered through computer-based testing.

The Technical and Safety examination contains 100 scored questions and allows five hours for completion. The Business examination contains 50 scored questions and allows two and one-half hours.

The Technical and Safety examination measures knowledge across a wide electrical-contracting scope. Candidates should be prepared to interpret electrical codes, fire-alarm standards, life-safety requirements, lightning-protection provisions, OSHA regulations, technical diagrams, equipment information, formulas, and practical installation scenarios.

National Electrical Code preparation may include conductor sizing, ampacity, raceway fill, box fill, services, feeders, branch circuits, grounding, bonding, overcurrent protection, motors, transformers, generators, emergency systems, legally required standby systems, special occupancies, special equipment, communications systems, and electrical signs.

Fire-alarm preparation may include initiating devices, notification appliances, alarm signals, supervisory signals, trouble signals, pathways, circuits, power supplies, emergency communications, documentation, inspection, testing, and maintenance.

Life-safety preparation may address occupancy classifications, occupant loads, means of egress, exit access, exits, exit discharge, travel distance, emergency lighting, fire-protection features, and electrical systems that support occupant protection.

Lightning-protection preparation may involve air terminals, conductors, bonding, grounding, surge protection, structural protection, installation methods, and inspection requirements.

OSHA preparation may include construction safety, general-industry safety, electrical hazards, personal protective equipment, fall protection, ladders, scaffolds, lockout and tagout, tools, hazard communication, injury and illness recordkeeping, and employer responsibilities.

Specialty-system preparation may include telecommunications wiring, structured cabling, electrical advertising signs, sign supports, sign foundations, neon tubing, electrodes, transformers, concrete mixtures, and technical electrical calculations.

The Business examination addresses contractor business responsibilities. Preparation may include business organization, financial management, contracts, project administration, employment matters, regulatory responsibilities, recordkeeping, and requirements affecting licensed Florida electrical contractors.

Open Book Test

The Florida Unlimited Electrical Contractor Technical and Safety examination is open book. Candidates may use authorized references that comply with the examination-room requirements for their scheduled testing period.

Only one copy of each approved reference may be used. Candidates should prepare with the editions assigned to their examination because questions are developed from the listed materials.

Open-book testing still requires extensive study. Five hours can pass quickly when a candidate is searching through a large technical library. Candidates should know which reference applies to each subject and how that book is arranged before test day.

The highlighted and tabbed books in this rental package support efficient navigation. Tabs provide access points to important chapters and code articles, while highlighting helps selected information stand out during review.

References may contain approved highlighting and underlining. Handwritten and typewritten notes are not permitted. Moveable tabs, removable page flags, loose sheets, sample questions, formulas, class notes, and unauthorized study materials should not be placed inside the books.

Candidates should practice using indexes, definitions, tables, annexes, chapter headings, exceptions, diagrams, and cross-references. Important answers may depend on a table note, exception, definition, or related section, so the complete applicable provision should be reviewed.

Useful timed lookup exercises include conductor ampacity, grounding-electrode requirements, raceway fill, box fill, motor calculations, transformer calculations, fire-alarm circuits, notification appliances, emergency lighting, means of egress, lightning-protection components, OSHA electrical safety, telecommunications pathways, neon installations, and sign-support requirements.

Licensing Steps

  1. Review the Certified Electrical Contractor classification. Confirm that the statewide electrical-contractor scope matches the work you intend to perform.
  2. Review the examination requirements. Prepare for the Technical and Safety examination and the separate Business examination.
  3. Apply for examination approval. Submit the applicable examination application to the Florida Electrical Contractors’ Licensing Board.
  4. Prepare with the rental package. Use the highlighted and tabbed references and complete the included online courses.
  5. Practice technical calculations. Review conductor sizing, services, feeders, motors, transformers, raceways, boxes, grounding, bonding, and related calculations.
  6. Practice open-book navigation. Learn which reference applies to each subject and complete timed lookup exercises.
  7. Schedule both examination parts. After receiving approval, schedule the computer-based testing appointments.
  8. Pass the required examinations. Complete both the Technical and Safety and Business examination requirements.
  9. Document qualifying experience. Prepare the electrical experience records required for initial licensure.
  10. Submit the licensing application. Provide the required experience, financial, insurance, background, and business documentation.

State Requirements

Applicants for the Florida Certified Electrical Contractor examination must be at least 18 years old. The state examination is offered in two parts, and both parts must be passed before an applicant can complete the initial licensure process.

Passing the examinations does not automatically issue a contractor license. Applicants must demonstrate that they meet the electrical experience requirements stated in the initial licensure application.

Current licensing requirements specify that the documented experience must include qualifying electrical work and that at least 40% of the experience must involve three-phase services.

Both examination scores must remain valid when the initial license application is submitted. The examination scores may not be more than three years old on the date of application.

The licensing process also requires a personal credit report. Applicants qualifying a business may need to provide a business credit report, a business financial statement, and additional records related to the company’s financial responsibility.

Insurance, background information, business records, and other supporting materials may also be required. The application used depends on whether the applicant is seeking an individual license, qualifying a business, or following another authorized licensing pathway.

A Certified Electrical Contractor may perform authorized electrical work throughout Florida. A registered electrical contractor is limited to the jurisdictions where the registration is held.
